thread.title: Manitoba government to establish trade representative office in India
thread.title_full: Manitoba government to establish trade representative office in India

author: First State Times
title: Manitoba government to establish trade representative office in India
text:
The Manitoba government will establish a regional trade representative in India as part of its efforts to diversify trading partners and expand market access, Business, Mining, Trade and Job Creation Minister Jamie Moses announced on May 20.
This move is intended to strengthen Manitoba’s economic ties with one of the fastest-growing economies in the world. The decision follows the province’s Economic Development Strategy announced in September 2025, which aims to build a resilient and competitive economy by expanding trade opportunities for Manitoba businesses and reducing reliance on the United States market.
“This is an important milestone for our province to develop closer ties with one of the fastest-growing economies in the world,” said Jamie Moses. “Having a permanent representative in the region will help build a relationship that will benefit Manitobans for decades to come.”
According to Moses, India’s rapidly growing middle class and consumer market present significant opportunities for Manitoba exporters. The new office is expected to provide market intelligence, foster business connections, attract investment, support trade missions and events, and report on outcomes that benefit Manitobans.
Chuck Davidson, president and CEO of the Manitoba Chambers of Commerce as well as co-chair of the Premier’s Business and Jobs Council trade diversification subcommittee said: “Manitoba businesses are increasingly looking beyond traditional markets to strengthen supply chains, expand exports and seize new economic opportunities. Establishing a dedicated Manitoba office in India is a welcome, strategic step that will help Manitoba businesses compete more effectively in global markets.”
More information about Manitoba’s Economic Development Strategy can be found at the Government of Manitoba .
